contentPlan.questionBrief: Ask builders what part of an AI agent is mostly theater and what part actually compounds.

contentDrafts.text: Tension: low nominal fees on a chain don’t equal good UX for real users. Tron’s cheap transactions are a marketing lever — but they hide three operational trade-offs teams keep ignoring. Non-obvious claim: if you’re building wallets or onboarding users on Tron, the single thing that predicts retention is not TRX price or block time; it’s how you handle resource provisioning (bandwidth/energy) + relay UX + liquidity access. Solve that triad and the rest is polish. Mechanism checklist…
pollOptions: Lack of on-chain liquidity / bridge pain
contentDrafts.imagePrompt: Minimalist technical diagram: three stacked blocks labeled Consensus (DPoS • Super Representatives), Resource Model (Bandwidth/Energy • freeze TRX), Liquidity (Pools & Bridges). Include a compact flow arrow showing: User signs intent -> Relayer tops up energy -> Tx submitted. Tron logo subtly placed. Color scheme: muted tech blues and grays, clear sans-serif labels, vector style, no people.
contentDrafts.rationale: Started with a tension and non-obvious claim to cut through marketing noise. Focused on mechanisms (resource model, relayer, liquidity) that materially affect wallet retention and are testable. Included a practical relayer pattern and specific metrics so builders can run experiments rather than argue about fees. Poll invites concrete diagnosis from operators. Image prompt supports the mechanism-first diagram and is actionable for a designer. Avoided hype, numbers, or fabricated claims; separated interpretive advice from factual bits about Tron’s consensus and resource model.
